TrendForce's latest report shows that Apple's smartphone production in the second quarter of 2026 grew 14% year-on-year, accounting for 19% of global production, second only to Samsung. The details are as follows.

The overall market decline was milder than previously expected.

In a report published today, TrendForce pointed out that Apple produced approximately 52 million iPhones in the second quarter of 2026, a 14% increase compared to the same period last year.

However, during the period, global smartphone production fell 8% year-on-year to 275 million units. TrendForce stated that the drop was "narrower than previously expected, with overall performance exceeding expectations".

In response to the new data, TrendForce revised its 2026 forecast, raising its global smartphone production estimate from the previous 1.05 billion units to 1.07 billion units. If ultimately confirmed, this would represent a 14% year-on-year decline, narrowing from the previously projected 16% drop.

Apple's performance was second only to Samsung. Samsung produced 62 million smartphones in the second quarter of 2026, a 7% year-on-year increase, accounting for 23% of global production.

Following Apple was Oppo, ranking third with 30 million units and an 11% market share (a 17% year-on-year decline); followed by Xiaomi with 29 million units and a 10% market share (-32%), vivo with 21 million units and an 8% market share (-18%), and Transsion with 20 million units and a 7% market share (-27%).

The report added that "a price increase for the upcoming iPhone 18 series seems inevitable, and its potential impact on sales momentum will be a key factor worth watching."

Finally, TrendForce also noted that the upward revision of its full-year 2026 forecast reflects consumers purchasing devices earlier, as well as manufacturers reversing some of their previously aggressive production cuts, rather than an increase in underlying demand.
